summary: I closed O-030, O-031 and O-032, and src/ is unchanged. For O-030 I first applied FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT in SourceInitialized, before the window is shown, and measured that this does not work. In height-3 and height-850 on real D:\, a window resized from 860 to 850 px still reproduced the whole scan-phase gap: 860 higher in 8 of 8 pairs, median 2.652. The cause is the window's first resize, not its height. The hook now sets the height as the window is made, in its Initialized event, before it has a handle, so no arm is ever resized. That event is reached through a Dispatcher.Hooks watch installed from the startup hook before Main. With it, 850 and 860 stall alike at the scan's first move (height-850-2: scan phase 3 of 8, median 0.952). The rerun 860-vs-644 batch (height-4) reads no-measurable-difference: 860 higher in 4 of 8 pairs, median 1.026, detectable 1.35x. I rewrote the findings record around this: I withdrew 'says yes' and the scan-phase follow-on, quoted the 850-vs-860 runs, and fixed the TreeMode comment. The batch driver now also removes the COMPlus_ aliases from each run's environment (O-031). A Trace batch now takes its sampling interval from its own traces' samplingNs rather than the reading's -SampleMs, and stops when traced runs disagree (O-032); three new fixtures and an arm-variables check cover these. This is the third attempt on the same point: where the hook sets the height (M1, then M3, then this attempt's own SourceInitialized version). This time the fix rests on a control batch (850 vs 860) that measures the arms equal, not on an argument about WPF's event order.

files.why: O-030. FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT is now set in the window's Initialized event, before it has a handle, or straight away if the window is already constructed with no handle. The window is reached from a Dispatcher.Hooks.OperationPosted watch (BeforeMain). The 'sized' line records 'when'. A window that already had its handle is refused. The Loaded-class-handler sizing is gone, along with its 'scanning' refusal, which could never fire (a code-review drift item). The comment now says what was measured.
Initialize calls TreeMode.BeforeMain in tree mode, so the dispatcher watch is in place before the app's Main creates the window.

O-031: $ArmVariables now covers the COMPlus_ forms (EventPipe*, EnableEventPipe). O-032: new Get-SampleRate takes the interval from the traced runs' own samplingNs, falls back to -SampleMs only when no stacks have one, and stops the reading (exit 1) on disagreement. The tracing-masks route to the 10 ms re-run applies below 10 ms. The self-test gains an expect.sampleMs check and an arm-variables check. The header is updated.
O-032: a 10 ms batch read again without -SampleMs is routed to the in-process fallback. Its recorded sampleMs is 10.
O-032: a 1 ms batch read again with -SampleMs 10 is still sent to the 10 ms re-run. Its recorded sampleMs is 1.
O-032: traced runs sampled at 1 ms and 10 ms stop the reading with exit 1.
The FSA_T005_HEIGHT comment now says the window is made at that height, before it has a handle. No behaviour change.

O-030. New section 'Four ways of setting the height': it quotes the code review's 850-vs-860 runs and height-3, height-850, height-4 and height-850-2, withdraws the scan-phase 'says yes' and its follow-on, and describes the first-resize observation. The Height verdict is now height-4's. The tools list covers COMPlus_ and the rate taken from the traces. The software-run sentence is corrected (a code-review drift item: those waits came on a later move). The follow-on and SL-044 sections are updated.

obligations.how: I set FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT in SourceInitialized first, before the window is shown, and measured that it still leaves the arms unequal. height-3 (860/644) and height-850 (860/850): scan phase 860 higher in 8 of 8 pairs, median 2.159 and 2.652. The height is now set as the window is made, in Initialized, so the handle is created at each arm's height and no arm is resized. All 34 runs of height-4 and height-850-2 logged 'when':'Initialized'. With the arms equal, 850 vs 860 stalls alike at the first move (336.8-500.8 vs 334.3-346.8 ms; scan phase 3 of 8, median 0.952). height-4 (860/644) reads no-measurable-difference: 4 of 8, median 1.026, sd 0.258, detectable 1.35. The doc quotes the code review's 850-vs-860 runs (224.4/224.3 vs 343.6 ms) and my own, states that the scan-phase difference followed the hook's resize, and withdraws 'says yes' and the scan-phase follow-on. The TreeMode comment (formerly :169-173) is rewritten to match.

$ArmVariables is now '^(FSA_T005_|FSA_HOOK_|(DOTNET|COMPlus)_(EventPipe|EnableEventPipe$)|DOTNET_STARTUP_HOOKS$)', and -match ignores case. The self-test's arm-variables check confirms 12 names are removed (COMPlus_EnableEventPipe, COMPlus_EventPipeConfig, a lower-case complus_eventpipeoutputstreaming, and the DOTNET_ forms among them). It also confirms 8 names are kept (TEMP, PATH, DOTNET_ROOT, COMPlus_gcServer, DOTNET_EnableEventPipeX and others). The header and doc list the COMPlus_ forms.

Get-SampleRate takes the interval from the traced runs' stacks (samplingNs / 1e6). It falls back to -SampleMs only when no stacks carry one. Traced runs that disagree stop the reading with exit 1 and a 'stopped' verdict. verdict.json records sampleMs and sampleMsFrom. Fixtures: reread-trace-rate-from-traces (a 10 ms batch read again without the flag goes to FSA_HOOK_MSGLOG, sampleMs 10), reread-trace-flag-ignored (a 1 ms batch read with -SampleMs 10 still goes to the 10 ms re-run, sampleMs 1) and trace-rates-disagree (exit 1). All pass; the first two would fail under the old code.

deviations: O-030 offered two fixes: apply the height before the window's first render, or give every arm the same load-time resize. I built the first at SourceInitialized (the window has a handle but is not yet shown) and measured it insufficient. height-3 and height-850 showed that any resize before the hook's first move, even one before the window is shown, takes the ~340 ms first-move stall away, so every arm except the XAML default's still differed. The built fix is a stricter form of the first option: the height is set before the window has a handle, so the handle is created at the arm's height and no arm is resized at all. The 850-vs-860 control (height-850-2) measures the arms equal.

To reach the window before it has a handle, the startup hook creates the main thread's Dispatcher (Dispatcher.CurrentDispatcher) before the app's Main. It then watches Dispatcher.Hooks.OperationPosted until MainWindow exists. This happens only in tree mode with FSA_HOOK_HEIGHT set. The app's Application adopts the same dispatcher. No other hook mode or plain launch changes.

The tracing-masks route to the 10 ms re-run now applies when the batch's rate is under 10 ms, not only at 1 ms or less. The header's rule has always said 'once more with -SampleMs 10', and a batch masked at, say, 5 ms had never been tried at 10.

I removed the 'scan had started before the hook sized the window' refusal. Code review recorded that it cannot fire, and under the new sizing no scan can have started. A refusal that can fire replaces it: the window already had its handle when the watch first saw it.
not_built: FSA_HOOK_MSGLOG, the in-process fallback, exists only as a contract. No Trace batch reached cannot-read or tracing-masks.

I did not re-run trace-2 and render-2 under the new sizing. Every run was at 860 px, where the old height set did nothing, and the one move at load was the same in both arms. Their 860 px first-move stall (333.6-343.9 ms) matches height-850-2's (334.3-346.8 ms).
A scan of D:\'s real contents and an elevated ETW/WPR capture remain open questions for a person (design-slice).
follow_ups: Run a Render batch of 8 pairs. render-2's 4 pairs could only have detected a 5.41x difference, so whether the SyncFlush wait is GPU- or present-side is not settled.

Measure where the first resize's cost goes when the window is resized once before it is shown, for example with a probe from before the window loads. In height-3 and height-850 that resize removed the ~340 ms from the hook's first move, which makes it the fix candidate this slice points to; nothing measured startup.
Run a traced batch of the ~1.3 s stall (the brief's 1,318.5 ms). In this attempt's batches it was the largest wait in 5 to 12 of 16 runs, in both arms, in the scan or the rescan.

Loop note: this is the third build attempt sent back over where the hook sets the height (M1, M3, and this attempt's own SourceInitialized version). This time the control batch (860 vs 850, height-850-2) settles it by measurement; a reviewer can check its runs rather than reason about WPF's event order.

D:\fsa-sl080-temp is still in place, as in attempt 1. artifacts/sl080 holds the superseded height-1/2/3 and height-850 batches beside height-4 and height-850-2 (gitignored; the doc marks which are superseded).
The code-review drift items not taken up here (the symmetric orderEffect flag; the Render rule's missing power floor) are still recorded under code-review.
